messages:
alex_sales: @joe_cust quick sync — Pioneer Health wants to run a Hybrid Private POC. main asks: preserve client src IP, support PrivateLink (interface endpoints) from on-prem through our edge proxy, and a clean firewall whitelist for egress. Can netops confirm feasibility and any blockers?

maria_netops: short answer: doable but two approaches. 1) PrivateLink to our NLB + proxy in customer's VPC (no client IP preserved unless you avoid SNAT). 2) TGW/NAT solution with static egress IPs if they must see preserved source IP. Need details about their TLS inspection and whether they require SNI passthrough or mTLS.

sam_solutions: adding context: we recommend PrivateLink for per-customer isolation and easier onboarding. For Pioneer they want to avoid changing on-prem NAT rules too much. If they insist on true client IP at application layer, we may need to terminate TLS at their proxy (mTLS) or use proxy protocol from our NLB -> their endpoint.

joe_cust: we prefer not to terminate TLS in the cloud. Our security team does TLS inspection in-house, so plaintext is not allowed. We also need to keep source IPs for logging.

maria_netops: ok. options then: (A) preserve source IP by keeping traffic on-prem until after TLS inspection: i.e., customer terminates TLS locally then forwards to Redwood over PrivateLink (would require their proxy to do egress to Interface Endpoint). (B) if traffic hits our NLB first, we'll see the NLB SNAT unless we enable proxy-protocol on the NLB + our edge accepts it — extra work. (C) use AWS Gateway Load Balancer / NLB with transparent proxy in their VPC — heavier.

alex_sales: timeline: Pioneer wants to start POC next week. What preflight items do we need to share with them to unblock-network? can we give them a minimal firewall/acl checklist and any static IPs?

infra-bot: FYI, Redwood Private POC uses regional egress IPs for outbound calls when behind our managed egress. Current POC IPs (region us-east-1): 34.120.45.12, 34.120.45.13, 34.120.45.14. These are subject to change for production.

maria_netops: checklist i'll send: - Preferred: Interface Endpoint (PrivateLink) to our NLB endpoint (TLS to our proxy). If customer must inspect TLS, they should terminate and re-encrypt before hitting Redwood. - If preserving client src-ip is required, customer should avoid SNAT between their proxy and our endpoint; consider using proxy-protocol or running a transparent pass-through proxy. - Egress firewall: allow outbound TCP 443 to our regional egress IPs (see infra-bot) and allow healthcheck ports from <their VPC CIDR> to our endpoint. - DNS: customer must create a private hosted zone / split-horizon entry pointing service.<customer>.redwood.internal -> interface endpoint ENI IPs.

sam_solutions: include a small SG example they can paste:
```
# example security group rules for customer proxy -> interface endpoint
- outbound: allow TCP 443 to 34.120.45.12/32, 34.120.45.13/32
- inbound: allow TCP 3000 from on-prem proxy subnet (if they run agent)
```

joe_cust: what's the recommended path for SNI? our firewall does SNI-based allowlist and we need SNI preserved.

maria_netops: PrivateLink preserves SNI (TLS handshake is end-to-end between client and service). If you do TLS termination in your proxy and re-encrypt to our endpoint, SNI on the second hop will be our hostname, so your inspection must capture original SNI beforehand. If you need us to accept the original SNI in headers, we can support passing the client SNI via an X-Forwarded-Host-ish header but that requires TLS termination at your side + mutual arrangement and is non-standard.

alex_sales: pricing/POC note: Pioneer asked if we charge extra for static egress IPs during POC. sam_solutions?

sam_solutions: For POC we don't bill for static IP assignment; egress bandwidth is part of trial credits. For Dedicated/Private in production, static egress is part of enterprise plan (small monthly add-on). I'll confirm exact numbers with finance but nothing blocking the POC.

joe_cust: one more blocker: our compliance wants to see an architecture diagram and a short network flow explaining where records stay and what crosses the internet. can you provide a one-pager?

maria_netops: will do. i'll sketch quick ASCII flow here for review then formalize:

Customer on-prem proxy -> (IPSec) -> TGW/Transit (optional) -> VPC Proxy (terminate TLS if required) -> Interface Endpoint (PrivateLink) -> Redwood NLB -> Redwood edge proxy -> Redwood inference cluster

Notes: if you keep TLS end-to-end, on-prem sees only TLS handshake and performs inspection pre-forward. If you need source-ip for app logs, avoid SNAT in the VPC proxy hop.

alex_sales: perfect. maria, can you drop the checklist + ascii diagram into a short doc and i'll forward to Pioneer. Also include the exact egress IPs and the small SG snippet.

maria_netops: will do, sending in ~30m. tagging @sam_solutions for pricing confirm. :thumbsup:

sam_solutions: confirmed with finance — POC static egress cover: $0, production reserved IPs: $500/mo. I'll add that to the doc.

joe_cust: thanks team. this helps a lot, will review once we get the doc and try to schedule ipsec setup for Tues.

alex_sales: awesome. next steps: maria to share doc; sam to confirm prod pricing email; joe to book IPsec handoff. closing thread after doc posted. :rocket:
